title: Vertical pricing sensitivity and latency arbitrage playbook
creator: Priya Sharma
description: Objective: quantify how customers across verticals respond to trade-offs between model price, latency, and quality; produce a playbook that converts those signals into routing and pricing controls for Redwood Runtime and Console. Motivation: as open model supply proliferates, our customers will trade lower per-token cost for higher latency or slight drops in quality. We need actionable elasticity curves and guardrails so Smart Routing and Optimize can make predictable decisions without causing regressions in end-user experience.
goals: Establish per-vertical elasticity curves for model substitution (price vs adoption)
Measure latency tolerance thresholds for latency-sensitive verticals (finance, enterprise search) vs cost-sensitive verticals (startups, batch embedding)
Produce a recommended routing policy matrix and telemetry signals to feed into automated rollouts and cost controls
Deliver a lightweight dashboard prototype for PM/SEs to explore tension between cost, latency, and quality per customer segment
success_metrics: Clear elasticity curve for >=5 representative verticals (SaaS search, customer support, fintech, e-commerce, content generation)
Signed-off routing policy matrix accepted by Runtime and Console teams
Dashboard demoed to 3 pilot customers and internal GTM teams
Reduction in per-token cost by 10-25% for pilot customers without measurable quality regressions (NPS/QA)
scope: Run a mix of lab experiments, passive telemetry analysis on a 3-month historical window, and 2 customer pilots. Produce a playbook with recommended default multipliers, latency arbitrage tolerance bands, and quality slippage thresholds. Integrate signals into the model selection decision spec (for runtime team) as a first-class input.
out_of_scope: Full automated pricing product or changes to public pricing; major infra refactors; onboarding more than 5 pilot customers in this phase.
research_plan: 1) Data pull: aggregate token-level usage, latency, and model chosen across hosted and dedicated customers for last 90 days (PM request to Analytics). 2) Lab ABs: run synthetic request workloads for representative prompts across 6 candidate models (cost-normalized) to measure latency vs quality. 3) Customer pilots: enable controlled routing on 2 enterprise and 1 startup customer with explicit guardrails. 4) Qualitative interviews with Solutions Eng and 4 customers to surface non-quantitative constraints.
deliverables: Elasticity spreadsheet with per-vertical curves and confidence intervals
Routing policy matrix (CSV) with recommended multipliers and fallback rules
Console dashboard prototype (Figma + basic dashboard link) and a telemetry query set
Playbook doc (Confluence link) with runbook for pilots, guardrails, and escalation paths
